# Deferred obligations ledger

> **Maintained companion — NOT a generated ticket.** This file is hand-maintained and committed. It
> is not produced by `decompose-spec` and must be **preserved across any ticket regeneration** — never
> overwritten or deleted. Rows are append-only (see rules below). It has no `NN_` sequence prefix
> precisely so it is not mistaken for a chain ticket.

Durable, in-repo record of **acceptance criteria and deliverables that a ticket could not fully
satisfy at implementation time** — almost always because they need a live GCP deploy or a HUMAN
prerequisite (Phase 0a / H0 etc.) that was not yet done. Each row names how it was proxied now, what
unblocks it, and exactly how to verify it when unblocked.

> **Machine ledger (build-memory v2, MAINT.1 / ADR-004):** the committed build state that reads these rows is
> `docs/build/LEDGER.md` (CURRENT STATE / OPEN FINDINGS / RETURN PASS / PHASE LOG); `docs/build/BUILD_INDEX.md`
> is one row per PR. `.agents/scratch/` is retired.

**This file is the source of truth for "what still owes verification."** It is read at the start of
every `implement-spec` run (via `AGENTS.md`). The rules:

1. **Every run, first:** read this file. If the ticket you are about to implement — or a prerequisite
   it depends on (e.g. H0 finishing, or an earlier ticket landing the egress-proxy SG) — unblocks any
   `OPEN` row, **closing that row is part of your run**: verify it for real, then flip it to `DONE`
   with the date and evidence (commit/PR).
2. **Never delete a row.** Flip `OPEN` → `DONE` (verified) or `WONTFIX` (with a reason). History stays.
3. **When you defer something new,** append a row here in the same run that defers it. A deferral that
   is not in this file did not happen.
4. **Backstop gates:** the phase-exit gates in `docs/tickets` (e.g. `16a_GATE-G1__phase0-exit.md`) must
   refuse to pass while any `OPEN` row scoped to that phase remains. Treat an open row as gate-blocking.

Status values: `OPEN` (owed) · `PARTIAL` (some of it landed; the rest still owed) · `DONE` (verified — add
date + evidence) · `WONTFIX` (add reason) · `ACCEPTED-SKELETON` (intentionally minimal for now; revisit at the
named ticket). A row's status is the first of these keywords that appears in its status cell (the rest of the
cell is free-form evidence prose).

| D-P0.15d-1 | **Reduced-rigor phase-set derivation in `buildHarnessRunSpec`.** With no explicit `phase` pin, the assembler derives the phase to run as `index === committed-phase count` over the FULL workflow manifest. For a REDUCED-rigor run (phases opted out via a manifest `optional` notch) this can select an opted-out phase and report the full `of`. | Deriving a run's ACTIVE phase set from its rigor (the §6.5/P0.06 rigor→`optOutFlag` mapping) is not available in the orchestrator yet, and the `optional: Rigor` semantics are not pinned; guessing risks the happy path | The §6.5 rigor→active-phase filter (P0.06/§6.5), or run-creation freezing the active phase list into `input_snapshot` | Filter the manifest to the run's active phases by rigor, derive the current phase + `of` from that list; assert a Quick/Standard run with an opted-out phase runs the next ENABLED phase | The default full-rigor run (the first-green milestone) is correct; an explicit `phase:"N"` pin is always honored (both tested, `runspec.test.ts`); only reduced-rigor auto-derivation is affected | **DONE (P0.15h Stage B, commit `0514679`).** `buildHarnessRunSpec` now selects the next phase by POSITION in the run's ACTIVE phase set — the manifest phases minus those whose `optOutFlag` is set `false` in the frozen inputs. Opted-out phases produce no committed step, so the committed-phase COUNT is exactly the next active phase's position; `of` stays the full manifest length so the delivery trigger (`phase.index === of-1`, keyed to the always-active final `letter`) is unaffected, and a `phase` pin still wins. ## PRB.20 — live ingestion + post-launch live-use findings

| id | obligation | why deferred | closes when | verification | evidence | status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| D-PRB.20-1 | **No concurrent-run guard — repeated run-sheet submissions spawn parallel runs + parallel holds.** The sheet mints `idempotencyKey` per GET render (`buildSheet` → `randomUUID()`), so the memo dedupe protects retries of ONE rendered submission but each sheet visit is a fresh intent; the api has no active-run check. Live result (operator, 2026-09-22): 4 review runs on `my-first-project` created 16:47:44–55Z, each holding 546 cr — 2,184 cr of a 2,500 balance held, 3 runs parked on unresolved `approve_scope` gates. | The concurrency question is a design ruling, not a mechanical fix: are parallel runs on one project ever legitimate (P1.06 scoped runs suggest per-scope parallelism may be)? The fix shape follows the ruling — an active-run guard in `createRun` (per project / per draft / per scope), the sheet showing "run in progress" instead of a fresh Run affordance, or both. | A ticket deciding the concurrency policy + implementing the guard (candidate: fold into P1.05/P1.06 run-card work, or a standalone PRB.2x defect ticket if the operator wants it sooner). | Submit the run sheet twice against the same project: second submit surfaces "run in progress" (or is rejected/redirected to the active run) per the ruling; assert no second hold lands in `credit_ledger`. | Live evidence: runs `01M35089QD…`, `01M3508D0Z…`, `01M3508EJS…`, `01M3508M00…` (2026-09-22, project `01M34YDZ3S…`) — 4× `review/quick`, 4× 546 cr holds; remediation = Stop on each of the 3 gate-parked dupes' `approve_scope` cards (cancels run + releases hold). | **DONE (2026-09-22, PRB.21)** — conservative beta ruling landed: at most ONE non-terminal run per project, enforced in `createRun` under a `select … for update` project-row lock (check-then-insert cannot race; memo dedupe precedes the guard so a same-key replay still returns its live run). Live on prod (update 69): two parallel `POST /projects/:id/runs` → 201 + **409 `run_in_progress`** carrying the active id; DB asserts ONE run row + ONE 36-cr `hold` (released on cancel); the sheet renders "in progress" + the `/review/<runId>` link with no Run affordance; `GET /projects` rows carry `activeRun`. Evidence: `docs/build/runs/PRB.21.md` § Stage B. |

## PRB.21 — post-launch live-use findings (day one cont.)

| id | obligation | why deferred | closes when | verification | evidence | status |
|----|------------|--------------|-------------|--------------|----------|--------|
| D-PRB.21-1 | **Estimator cap model cannot complete a real `review` run — verification-phase research burn is unmodeled.** The cap is enforced on proxy-metered burn (all SDK requests incl. research fetches' context), while the estimate tracks committed-debit rates. Live result (operator, 2026-09-22): FIVE consecutive `cap_reached` deaths across three rigor levels on two docs — `01M3508M` quick est 364/cap 546 → died 622; `01M35CEQ…` standard est 1657/cap 2486 → died 2629; `01M35FR9…` quick est 73/cap 110 → died 119; `01M35HHJ6…` quick est 73/cap 400 → died 407; `01M35KCFA…` quick est 73/cap 400 → died 466 on a 701-word draft with **zero fetchable URLs** (`fetch_log`: 128 fetches + 13 searches — verification does its own web research per claim regardless of in-doc citations; `usage_records`: 6.65M cache-read tokens / 41 calls). Meanwhile committed debits stayed modest (intake ~102, craft ~87–122). The one completed quick review (`01M2TZ8E`, cap 390, spent 146) predates the fetch-heavy verification profile — and quick's honest floor (est ~57–73 → cap ~86–110) sits BELOW minimum viable burn (~146+), so quick rigor is structurally uncompletable at derived caps. | The fix is a design ruling with real product/economic consequences: bound the research (per-claim/per-run fetch+search budget, fetched-page truncation/context discipline), model the burn (research addend in the estimator driven by claim count), and/or re-scope what the cap meters. Not a drive-by patch. | A ticket that picks the fix shape and lands it (candidate `28m_PRB.22`), then proves a real review DELIVERS within its derived cap on prod. | One bounded live `review` run on a small doc: assert `state=delivered`, `spent_credits ≤ cap_credits`, committed debits ≈ estimate, and fetch/search counts within the chosen budget. | Run ids above + ledger rows (holds 110/400/546/2486 → releases after debits 58/190/224/~158/536); `fetch_log`/`usage_records` counts from `rhema` prod DB 2026-09-22; ~$11.7 committed across the day's attempts. | **DONE — 2026-09-23 (delivered; residual pricing-model question stays OPEN for G3 below). History — 2026-09-22 PRB.22 sharpened it, then corrected it:** the research bound shipped live (per-run `webTools{fetchBudget:24,searchBudget:11,fetchMaxContentTokens:8000}` propagated to the proxy credential + estimator research addend → derived cap 207) but the one sanctioned verify run `01M35Q8M…` still died `cap_reached` at 211 — with **zero** fetches/searches made. Post-mortem usage analysis: ~34 requests × ~66K–1M cache-read tokens each ≈ 5.1M cache-read on a 1K-token doc — the burn is **baseline harness context churn** (protocol prompts + accumulated turns per request), independent of doc size or research. Correction to the earlier note: the "completed precedent" `01M2TZ8E` was a `fact_check` run (not review) and itself burned ~5.8M cache-read/~430cr usage — the pattern is inherent, and **no `review` run has ever delivered on prod within a derived cap**. Real fixed overhead ≈ 400–850cr burn per run; the estimator models content size, not request-count × context-size. Remaining work: context-management (per-phase fresh context / per-claim subagent isolation / prompt slimming) + a phase-count × per-phase-floor estimate model, OR an explicit product ruling on real per-run cost (~$4–8.50 burn) vs advertised estimate. **2026-09-23 addendum (PRB.23 Stage B):** sixth `cap_reached` death — `01M35Y9BH…` review/quick on the same zero-URL draft, deployed with the −45% request-envelope cut, frozen phase toggles, and the 50cr/phase churn term (derived est 288 / cap 432, no operator raise). Died in `verification` at proxy-metered 506 (committed debits only 159); usage: 5.03M cache-read over 44 calls (~60K/request to the editor loop), 13 fetches / 3 searches, 2 compactions. Confirms the residual is **per-phase transcript accumulation** — smaller per-request envelopes don't bound transcript growth; the churn term priced but under-modeled verification (≈347cr actual vs 50 priced). Next lever is context resets/per-claim isolation or a product cost ruling, not further envelope work. **2026-09-23 RESOLVED — `01M36663QG1ZJ7VEZ036Y54NSG` DELIVERED:** review/quick on draft 6 `completed` at 04:25Z, metered 720 ≤ operator cap 1100 (derived est 522/cap 783 — synthesis-phase `letter` burn still needed ~300cr of headroom above the derived cap; the derived cap alone would have died at 783 again). All phases done: intake 79, craft 70, verification 233 (bounded — first completion), argument 84, letter 120; committed debits 586 ($5.86); usage 104 reqs / 13.3M cache-read, 26f/27s, 1 compaction. **Residual sharpened, not closed:** the honest delivered cost of a 701-word quick review is ~720cr metered (~$7.20) vs sheet-advertised ~73cr-era pricing — the derived-cap vs delivered-cost gap (783 vs 720 marginal) and the committed-vs-metered delta (586 vs 720) remain the open pricing-model question for G3; synthesis-phase churn is still under-modeled (letter needed ~241 metered vs 120 committed). **2026-09-25 (RCN.1):** row stays DONE (the blocker — no real `review` could complete under the cap model — is resolved: `01M36663…` delivered). The residual pricing-model question is real but is *new* scope, not this row's AC; it rides **STB.3**'s bounded runs as metered-vs-committed data (and a future pricing-model ticket if STB.3's data confirms the gap). **2026-09-26 (STB.3 data):** the gap is confirmed alive — tonight committed 451cr vs 1,304cr metered (cancelled runs commit only completed-phase debits; `runs.spent_credits` carries the reconciled metered truth — §4-F5).
